narrative:
Your loan application was reviewed by our credit assessment system, which evaluated your financial profile and determined a 54% likelihood of credit risk — a figure just above the threshold that led to the denial of your application. While this is not an overwhelming margin, it was sufficient to flag your application as a potential risk, and understanding the specific reasons behind this outcome may help you take steps to improve your situation.

The single most influential factor working against your application was your credit history. You were recorded as having "no credits or all paid," which might sound positive at first glance, but it actually signals to the assessment system that there is very little evidence of how you manage ongoing credit obligations over time. Among applicants who were approved, the vast majority — over 85% — had a track record of existing paid credits or even some past difficulties that were resolved, both of which provide a clearer picture of repayment behavior. Without that history, your application carries more uncertainty, and uncertainty tends to be interpreted as risk.

The second most important factor was the status of your checking account, which currently holds between 0 and 200 Deutsche Marks. This relatively modest balance raised concerns about your financial cushion, especially since more than half of approved applicants had no checking account obligations at all or maintained healthier balances. A limited checking account balance can suggest that there is little financial buffer available if unexpected expenses arise during the repayment period.

On a more positive note, the fact that you own real estate actually worked in your favor and helped offset some of the negative signals. Property ownership is viewed as a sign of financial stability and provides a form of security, and this factor pushed the assessment in a more favorable direction — though not enough to overcome the concerns raised by your credit history and account status.

There are also a few other aspects of your profile worth noting: you are currently employed for less than a year and renting your home, both of which are less common among approved applicants, and your job classification as unemployed or unskilled non-resident is a category shared by fewer than 2% of those who were approved. These factors, while not the primary drivers of the decision, likely contributed to the overall picture.

To improve your chances in the future, the most impactful step you can take is to build a demonstrable credit history — for example, by taking out a small, manageable credit line and repaying it consistently over time. Strengthening your checking account balance and, if possible, securing more stable long-term employment would also significantly improve your profile. We encourage you to reapply once these aspects of your financial situation have had time to develop.
